example_prompt: What is the status of checkout session {id}?

status.description:
`PENDING`: created, not confirmed yet (customer on the page, OTP pending, redirection in progress).
`SUCCESS`: confirmed by the aggregator. `FAILED`: refused or failed at the operator, the customer can retry on the same session.
`CANCELLED`: cancelled, no longer payable. `REFUNDED`: refunded from the dashboard.

livemode.description: `true` for a production object, `false` for a test object: created with a test key, or in a workspace not switched live yet. Verify webhook signatures with the secret key of the same mode.

oneOf.description: Your own free-form data, returned in webhooks. Cartflox adds `source` (`checkout_session`, `widget`, `payment_link`...) and, when relevant, `description`, `success_url`, `cancel_url` and `idempotencyKey`.

application.description: Name of the mobile application to open, when relevant.

oneOf.description: What the buyer still has to do (enter a code, dial a USSD code, follow a redirection), when the provider said so only after the initiation.

completed_at.description: Confirmation date, `null` until the payment succeeds.

failure_message.description: Why the payment failed, as told by the provider and translated.

provider_reference.description: Reference at the aggregator, for your reconciliations.

error_schema.description: Error body. `code` is present on transfer endpoints.

gotchas: The redirect to success_url can happen before the operator confirms: only this endpoint's status (or the webhook) is authoritative, so check it server-side before delivering.
Polling is throttled: while the session is PENDING, Cartflox re-checks the aggregator at most once every 8 seconds per session, so polling more often does not give fresher payment information.
FAILED is not a final state: the customer can retry on the same session, so a FAILED status should not cancel the order by itself.
